name: Exact Dominance-Defect Law under Boolean Substitution
statement: If $T$ is proper and nonempty and the outer sections satisfy $C_0\ne C_1$, then $d_{\rm dom}(C\circ_iT)=\max\{d_{\rm dom}(C),d_{\rm dom}(T)\}$. If $C_0=C_1=B$, the output is $B\times\{0,1\}^Y$ and has defect $d_{\rm dom}(B)=d_{\rm dom}(C)$. For a full or empty test, a nonempty output has the defect of $C_0$ or $C_1$, respectively.
proof: When both inputs have zero defect, combine their strict dominance certificates in a two-control extension, scale the outer gaps beyond the bounded inner control weights, use a common outside witness at shared heights, and complete the redundant rows by strict resolution. Projection gives the substitution and preserves zero defect. Conversely, a crossing test edge recovers $C$ as a minor, while a word in $C_0\triangle C_1$ recovers $T$ or its complement; minor monotonicity gives both reverse inequalities. Boundary cases are products and sections.
comments: No positive-value formula for $\tau$ and no general realizable-ample substitution closure is claimed.
